info.name: warframeRelic
info.description:
Every endpoint Relic Finder serves, grouped by the question it answers.

baseUrl is http://localhost:8080 — the backend's own port, which is what a checkout and the Docker compose both expose. Behind nginx on port 80 the same paths work under http://localhost.

Endpoints addressed by name want the FULL name: /api/relics/relic/Lith%20V9 answers 200, /api/relics/relic/V9 answers 404.

Five of these are not reads. POST /api/relics/update rebuilds the catalogue, POST /api/refresh/{view} re-reads the source behind one ranked view, POST /api/app/update/install replaces this copy of the application, and the two PUTs replace a stored list whole.

item.name: Catalogue
item.description: What exists: relics, what is inside them, where they drop, and what is still farmable. Nothing here touches warframe.market.

request.description: Every relic in four states — Intact, Exceptional, Flawless, Radiant — with the six rewards and the chance each carries at that refinement.
The same catalogue as a map: era, then refinement, then the relics.
One era at a time: lith, meso, neo or axi. 404 when the era holds nothing.
All four states of one relic. The full name is required: /api/relics/relic/V9 answers 404.
The missions that drop this relic, with the rotation and the chance. A relic that is vaulted drops nowhere and answers an empty array, which is why the example is one still in rotation.
true or false, and nothing else.
Every relic still dropping in the game right now, grouped by era.
Every relic that holds that Prime part. 404 when no relic does.

item.name: Where a set sits in its cycle

request.description: For each Prime set: whether it still drops from relics, how long ago it stopped, and where that puts it in its price cycle.
Rebuilds the catalogue from drops.warframestat.us. This is the relic catalogue, NOT the application — see GET /api/app/update for that one.

item.name: Prices
item.description: warframe.market, through a server-side cache and one rate limiter. The market allows about three requests a second, which is why the bulk endpoints exist: firing the single-item one forty times gets the caller throttled.

request.description: Average, median, trades and trend for a single Prime part.
The series behind the price chart. warframe.market keeps it, so nothing is stored on this side.
Up to 5000 part names in one call. An item with no listing comes back with a null price rather than being dropped, so the response lines up with the request.

body.raw:
[
  "Volt Prime Chassis",
  "Volt Prime Neuroptics",
  "Volt Prime Systems"
]

request.description: A relic and a part of the same name are two different listings on the market, and the slug differs — a relic's ends in _relic.
The same series, for a sealed relic.
Every row of the relics table in one call. Same null-rather-than-dropped rule as /items.
Predates /api/market/relic/{name} and answers an average with no trade count. New callers want that one instead.
The cache fills in the background over a few minutes. This is what the page reads to say so, rather than showing a table full of dashes.
A diagnostic: the items whose price is re-read more often than the default rule would, and how much drift each is allowed. It answers 'why is this item read hourly', which an interval alone cannot.
A hint, not a request for data: the tables go on asking for the whole catalogue, and this says which rows someone is actually looking at so those are priced first. Answers 204 whatever happens.

item.name: Rankings
item.description: The three views that answer a question with a number, and the one door that makes those numbers newer.

request.description: Every relic banded S to F, twice: once for opening it alone and once for a radshare. The bands are drawn around the median of the population asked for, so vault moves them with it; limit cuts the response and never the population. Answers an ETag, so polling it costs a 304 and no body. A misspelled parameter is a 400 naming what it accepts.
Sell orders from sellers who are online, best Endo per platinum first, computed from the stars actually socketed in that specific sculpture.
An ISO instant, or null before the first read. Its own endpoint because /offers is parsed as a bare array by everything that asks for it.

ducats, endo or tiers. Re-reads the source behind that view — the drop tables and the item database for ducats and tiers, the Ayatan orders for endo — and never the ~1500 cached prices. Each source carries a cooldown, so asking twice inside the window is one re-read and one refusal, and the answer says when it may be asked again. A source that did not answer still comes back 200, carrying source-unavailable.

item.name: Your lists
item.description: Plain JSON files under data/, no database and no accounts: the service is single-tenant, so whoever runs it owns the only list. Both PUTs REPLACE the whole list — firing one with the example body below overwrites what is stored.

request.description: Every line, with the kind that says what it is for: part, set, relic, ducat or endo. The same part can appear twice under two kinds, and that is two lines rather than a conflict.
Replaces it whole. Send back what GET returned, changed — an empty array empties the list.
Name and count. A count rather than a bare name because a set is not one copy of each piece.
Replaces it whole, same as the wishlist.

item.name: The application itself
item.description: These talk to GitHub rather than to Warframe, and one of them changes the machine.

request.description: Reads a constant: local, immediate and free. It is what a page waiting out an update polls once a second — a different answer than before the server went away means the new copy is up.

200 even with no network — known: false and nothing else filled — because a machine that is offline is an ordinary state and not a server error. Cached for an hour, so two calls in a row are one request outward.

The one that changes the machine. A Windows install downloads the release's setup, verifies it against the sha256 GitHub publishes and only then runs it. Everything else is refused with not-supported, a container included: a container is recreated from outside by whoever runs the daemon.
Polled while it works. It also answers before anybody starts, which is how a page knows whether an install is already running.
